title: webwrite
summary: Write data to a web service and decode its response.

gpu_support.notes: HTTP execution is host-side. Automatically resident values gather transparently; explicit gpuArray input requires RunMat mode.

description: `webwrite` sends data to an HTTP or HTTPS service and decodes the response according to its content type and options.
behaviors: The first input is an absolute URL supplied as a character vector or string scalar.
Post names are text. Post values may be text, numeric, logical, or datetime values, including supported arrays; native integer values are serialized from exact storage.
A structure or supported numeric value may be used as JSON data. Nested native integer values remain exact through JSON serialization.

A final options structure controls `ContentType`, `MediaType`, `Timeout`, `HeaderFields`, `Username`, `Password`, `UserAgent`, and `RequestMethod`. The default timeout is 5 seconds, and an integer timeout is read exactly.
`ContentType` controls how the response is parsed (`"auto"` by default). Set it to `"json"`, `"text"`, or `"binary"` to force JSON decoding, text return, or raw byte vectors.

`MediaType` sets the outbound `Content-Type` header. When omitted, RunMat chooses a sensible default (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `application/json`, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, or `application/octet-stream`) based on the payload.

RunMat additionally supports `QueryParameters`, direct option-like name-value pairs, and raw byte-oriented uploads. These conveniences are distinct from the portable post-pair plus final-options form.
HTTP errors, timeouts, TLS verification problems, and JSON encoding issues raise MATLAB-style errors with descriptive text.

examples.description: Posting form fields to a REST endpoint
Supplying credentials, custom headers, and query parameters

faqs.question: Which HTTP methods are supported?
faqs.answer: `webwrite` defaults to `POST`. Supply `"RequestMethod","put"` (or `"patch"`, `"delete"`) to use other verbs.

faqs.question: How do I send JSON?
faqs.answer: Set `"MediaType","application/json"` (optionally via a struct) or `"ContentType","json"`. RunMat serialises the payload with `jsonencode` and sets the appropriate `Content-Type`.

faqs.question: How are form posts encoded?
faqs.answer: Struct inputs and two-column cell arrays are turned into `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies. Field values must be scalar text or numbers.

faqs.question: Can I post binary data?
faqs.answer: Yes. Provide numeric tensors (`double`, integer, or logical) and set `"ContentType","binary"` or `"MediaType","application/octet-stream"`. Values must be in the 0–255 range.

faqs.question: What controls the response decoding?
faqs.answer: `ContentType` mirrors `webread`: `"auto"` inspects response headers, while `"json"`, `"text"`, and `"binary"` force the output format.

faqs.question: How do I add custom headers?
faqs.answer: Use `"HeaderFields", struct("Header-Name","value",...)` or a two-column cell array. Header names must be valid HTTP tokens.

faqs.question: Does `webwrite` follow redirects?
faqs.answer: Yes. The underlying `reqwest` client follows redirects with the same credentials and headers.

faqs.question: Can I send query parameters and a body simultaneously?
faqs.answer: Yes. Provide a `QueryParameters` struct/cell in the options. Parameters are percent-encoded and appended to the URL before the request is issued.

faqs.question: How do timeouts work?
faqs.answer: `Timeout` accepts a positive numeric scalar up to 2147.483647 seconds or `Inf`. The default is 5 seconds.

faqs.question: What happens with GPU inputs?
faqs.answer: Automatically resident values gather transparently before serialization. Explicit gpuArray input is a named RunMat extension and is rejected before provider access in MATLAB-compatible mode.

gpu_residency: Requests and results are host-side. Automatically resident values gather transparently; explicit gpuArray input requires RunMat mode.
gpu_behavior: The request path terminates fusion and gathers automatically resident values through their owning provider. Explicit gpuArray input crosses the `webwrite-explicit-gpu-input` extension gate before any gather.
